distinguishing_from: CANONICAL login wall: the request URL and the final URL differ, and the final URL contains a return parameter pointing back at the original. That redirect-with-return-param shape is the single most reliable login signal in this corpus.
notes: HTTP 200 at the END of the chain. Status code is useless; the redirect chain is everything.

markers: <title>Login or Sign Up for a Dropbox Account</title>
distinguishing_from: Same shape as github_settings (302 to /login with a continuation param). body_text_chars is 38, near zero, because the login UI is client-rendered, so an emptiness heuristic would confuse this with a broken page.
notes: Best example of a login wall whose HTML carries almost no text. Classify from the Location header and the title, not the body.

distinguishing_from: vs http_404: a nonexistent DOI was requested, and instead of 404 the site redirected twice to a SESSION-COOKIE interstitial and returned 200. Neither the requested resource's absence nor a login requirement is stated anywhere.
notes: IMPORTANT EDGE CASE. The same host returned a normal 200 article for a valid DOI in this same run, so /action/cookieAbsent is not a blanket wall. Demonstrates that one host can serve several wall types depending on path validity and cookie state.

distinguishing_from: WEAK SAMPLE, kept deliberately. This is a browser-capability interstitial that also offers sign-in, not a true auth redirect. A classifier keying on 'Sign in' alone will call this login_required; keying on a redirect-with-return-param will correctly not.
notes: HTTP 200, no redirect, 912 visible-text chars. Use as a hard case rather than a clean positive.
